nodes.title: `net.isOnline()`/`net.online` always returns `true` when called from module running as a utility process.
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Sequoia 15.6

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Using Electron's [`net`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/net) module, calling `net.isOnline()` or `net.online` within a module that's running as a utility process should reflect the actual state of the host device.

### Actual Behavior

When I've disconnected wifi on the device and call `net.isOnline()` from within the utility process module, the result is `true`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/achou11/159165d915505372f1450177757e9aa8

### Additional Information

The gist shows the disparity between what can be determined within different processes i.e. renderer vs main vs utility. The renderer uses the [NetworkInformation API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/NetworkInformation) while the main and utility processes use Electron's [`net`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/net) module

When running the reproduction while disconnect from wifi, you'll noticed that the renderer and main log the expected results, whereas the utility process logs an unexpected result.

nodes.title: Deep Links launch second instance - only when installed via the Microsoft App Store (appx)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

36.7.4

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

After the login in the default browser, clicking the link (or being redirected) to the custom url scheme, the same instance should be focused, and the "second-instance" event fired, since we have requested a lock with `requestSingleInstanceLock()` and the deep link is registered with `setAsDefaultProtocolClient(...)`. 
**Note:** This does all work correctly, and as expected - **BUT** only when the application is installed via the unsigned .appx file (that electron-builder can produce). The same for nsis (.exe installer)

### Actual Behavior

A second instance is created. The Task Manager shows both the `myapp.exe` files running - the originally opened one, and the second instance with the parameter. `myapp.exe?param=val`
**Again:** This does not happen in testing, or development. It only happens when the installer "myapp-setup.appx" file is downloaded from the Microsoft Store.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Confirm FFmpeg Configuration for Electron v35.2.0 Regarding LGPL and Codec Usage
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

35.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows, Linux

### Operating System Version

Windows 10, RedHat Linux 8

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

35.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Description: 
We are evaluating the use of Electron v35.2.0 (downloaded from https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v35.2.0/electron-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip) 
Then download ffmpeg.dll (downloaded from https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v35.2.0/ffmpeg-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip)
To replace the same file from Electron v35.2.0 for ensuring under LGPL-2.0.
Our legal and compliance team has specific requirements regarding FFmpeg usage:

- If FFmpeg is used, it must be entirely under an LGPL license (no GPL components).
- FFmpeg must not include any Audio or Video Codecs; all codec functionality must be implemented by underlying Hardware or OS (e.g., GPU or Windows Media Foundation).

The prebuilt `ffmpeg.dll` in the v35.2.0 ZIP includes a `LICENSES.chromium.html` file stating FFmpeg is under LGPL-2.1+, which aligns with the LGPL requirement. However, we need confirmation on the following:
1. Does the FFmpeg in v35.2.0 use `ffmpeg_branding = "Chrome"` and `proprietary_codecs = false` as per the default build? build/args/ffmpeg.gn
2. Are there any software-implemented Audio or Video Codecs (e.g., H.264, AAC) included in the prebuilt `ffmpeg.dll`?
3. If software codecs are included, can we disable them in the prebuilt version, or must we rebuild ffmpeg from source to exclude them?

Steps to Reproduce
1. Download `electron-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip` from the release page.
2. Extract and inspect `ffmpeg.dll` and `LICENSES.chromium.html`.
3. Download `ffmpeg-v35.2.0-win32-x64.zip` from the release page.
4. To replace the same file from Electron v35.2.0 for ensuring under LGPL-2.0.

Expected Behavior
- FFmpeg should be LGPL-2.1+ compliant with no GPL components.
- No software-implemented Audio or Video Codecs should be present; codec support should rely solely on Hardware/OS.

### Additional Information
- Electron version: v35.2.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (x64)
- Compliance deadline: September 1, 2025
- Contact: oyeh@lenovo.com

We kindly request the Electron team's assistance in verifying the FFmpeg configuration or providing guidance on disabling software codecs while maintaining LGPL compliance. If rebuilding is required, please advise on the necessary GN flags (e.g., `proprietary_codecs = false`, `ffmpeg_branding = "Chromium"`).

Thank you!

### Actual Behavior

- `LICENSES.chromium.html` confirms LGPL-2.1+, but codec usage is unclear.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: File picker allows selecting directories if their name includes a file extension
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.2.6

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15.5

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

The file picker (`<input type=file>`, `showOpenFilePicker`) should not allow selecting directories, only files.

### Actual Behavior

The file picker allows selecting directories if they match some of the given file extensions. The directory is exposed to JS as a File / FileSystemFileHandle, but fails to be read.

For example, the following code:

```
window.showOpenFilePicker({
    multiple: true,
    types: [
      {
        accept: {
          "application/octet-stream": [".foobar"],
        },
      },
    ],
  });
```

allows choosing directories named with ".foobar" even though they are not files. Trying to read the file fails with an unclear error message.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be8129a5-5eb8-4b73-a939-b266687faa6a

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/jtbandes/98f048be7671b36105e656939c64d633

### Additional Information

I have also filed an issue upstream with Chrome at https://issues.chromium.org/issues/438779953

However, I have noticed that Electron already has some custom behavior around file picking of directories (see below), so I am also filing a bug here, in case it makes sense to add any workarounds or patches to Electron.

- Related: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8948
  - closed by https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/9834
- Related: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/13219
  - closed by https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/13220
- Related: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/24755
  - closed by https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/25030

nodes.title: more video formats
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I have a use case where I need to "natively" play MKV, AVI, FLV, and other video formats that are usually unsupported by browsers, with support for audio tracks and subtitles. Due to the way Electron.js is built, and from what I have found over several days of research, I know that there is no native support for such formats and features. However, I believe this can be added more effectively than if it were done by a developer with less technical capability (like myself).

although I am looking at this from my own case, I believe that having this capability could be enriching, even for other types of projects.

### Proposed Solution

implementing support for the mentioned video formats (and others) through a more "native" approach that does not create much additional processing overhead, while being able to leverage hardware resources that, at best, Electron.js is better equipped to utilize.

### Alternatives Considered

integration with players like VLC and real-time transcoding. Both possibilities have been considered and attempted, but since I am not the most experienced developer for this type of process, I encountered significant performance issues (as I need to cater to PCs with modest configurations) and some security gaps.

### Additional Information

electron.js has been great for addressing various use cases over the years, and I believe that adding this native support will open up many possibilities for many developers. please consider this! thank you!

### Electron Version

36.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

29.4.6

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When the same browserView is added to a browserWindow multiple times, the visibility of the pages in the browserView does not change.

### Actual Behavior

When the same browserView is added to a browserWindow multiple times, the visibility of the pages in the browserView quickly changes from visible to hidden and then to visible.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/mai-121/43a7ad52f16e6c86b0fc1369c84fa97a

### Additional Information

After the BrowserView module was refactored in Electron 30, the behavior of the addBrowserView API changed. When the same browserView is added multiple times to a browserWindow, the browserView will first be removed and then re-added.
Specifically, this causes a jump in the page's visibility inside the browserView, and the visibilitychange event is triggered unexpectedly.

The impl of  'addBrowserView'  in different versions:
electron 29: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v29.4.6/shell/browser/api/electron_api_base_window.cc#L762
electron 30: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v30.0.0/lib/browser/api/browser-window.ts#L178

_No response_

nodes.title: NodeJS module-sync target support
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

## Introduction
I know this is a high traffic issue so i will justify that i know what i say.
I am aware of the ESM Support electron dlopen and i am v8 engineer i am aware of intrinsic and embedding node inside chrome. i know all Electron ESM issues i understand that some settings need to get exported Sync before the embedding gets used.

### Feature Use Case

There is a new import condition for NodeJS called 'module-sync' it is the missing block to require ESScripts see: module-sync in https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#conditional-exports

"module-sync" - matches no matter the package is loaded via import, import() or require(). The format is expected to be ES modules that does not contain top-level await in its module graph - if it does, ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE will be thrown when the module is require()-ed.

so it is able to be seen as ideal forward migration for all existing CJS code. I guess this will work also for embedding.

### Proposed Solution

Electron can default and exclusiv use the ModuleSync target. Fun fact the same Implementation gets used to enable module service workers in chrome. They also can not contain TLA.

## Bonus.
good solution to detect it:

--experimental-print-required-tla[#](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--experimental-print-required-tla)
Added in: v22.0.0, v20.17.0
If the ES module being require()'d contains top-level await, this flag allows Node.js to evaluate the module, try to locate the top-level awaits, and print their location to help users find them.

--experimental-require-module

### Alternatives Considered

all alternatives are in the old ESM issues you know them start with .cjs then use import or use esm npm package which is a sync ESM loader Implemented in CJS .............

### Additional Information

_No response_
